events.title: What is PHP and how serious is the computer language flaw causing website shutdowns?
events.summary: An estimated 70% of websites use the open-source language. What is the identified vulnerability in it? Website owners faced millions of attempts to exploit a serious security vulnerability in their programming language, it has emerged, triggering a rush by governments and businesses to fix the problem. The newly discovered vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language that underpins most websites, allows hackers to carry out cyber-attacks and steal data if not fixed. What were the vulnerabilities and why did they affect so many sites? PHP is an open-source scripting language that is more than 30 years old and used across much of the internet. Content management systems and publishing template systems such as Wordpress are built on PHP. An estimated 70% of websites use PHP, with millions of sites affected by the vulnerabilities. Wikipedia and Facebook are among those. In the UK alone, the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) sent out 50,000 alerts to organisations with affected systems, while government websites in France, the Netherlands, Canada, Japan and Germany were taken down temporarily as a precaution while a fix was added. According to the PHP Foundation , the not-for-profit that maintains PHP code, the issues “sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: memory management and error handling”. The two vulnerabilities were labelled by the security vendor Hadrian as a “PHP2Shell exploitation”. The vulnerabilities work by corrupting the memory in a website through a request that can then be used to launch an attack and could “provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database”, according to the US National Security Agency. Historically, researchers and cybersecurity experts would test systems for vulnerabilities and patch the issues when they were discovered – or patch when one system was attacked and a vulnerability was identified. Artificial intelligence has now sped up this process as AI can be thrown at systems to identify potential issues that might not have been spotted by a human, and can do so in a much shorter time frame. The PHP Foundation said it had worked with Anthropic’s frontier model to scan its code, and had PHP put into OpenAI’s Patch the Planet program, which discovered the issue at the same time as a researcher, Ryan A, in mid-August. The disclosure of the vulnerabilities had been embargoed until 22 October, to give websites time to fix it. But according to the PHP Foundation, it discovered the two vulnerabilities had begun circulating on forums and social media on Tuesday and so brought forward the disclosure. The UK’s NCSC said this had created a 12- to 14-hour window for people to look for the vulnerability in websites before they could be patched. The breadth of the vulnerability appears to be unprecedented. As the PHP Foundation has said, the issues sit in parts of PHP that nearly every request touches: “Their central place in PHP is what made both vulnerabilities serious, and also so hard to fix without breaking compatibility, hurting performance, or forcing changes on the large ecosystem of third-party extensions.” Coupled with the sheer number of sites that rely on PHP, that makes it a massive problem that should be fixed as soon as possible. Now the flaw is out in the wild, Hadrian said it was seeing “exploitation happening at scale”. However, so far no major hacks appear to have occurred. In the 24 hours since the vulnerability was announced, the NCSC said it had not seen any successful hacks. Patches are already available, and the reason a number of websites went down in the past few days was that people were working to patch their systems immediately. A number of the websites returned quickly. Security companies have recommended patching straight away, and where it cannot be done immediately, systems should be taken offline. “Shutting down a service for a few hours costs far less than a compromised server,” Hadrian said. However, it will depend on businesses and governments being aware they need to patch, and doing so quickly. “The immediate challenge is not simply installing a patch, but finding and managing every instance where PHP is running,” said Don Smith, the vice-president of threat intelligence at the cybersecurity firm Sophos Counter Threat Unit. Sigi Goode, a professor of information systems at the Australian National University, said the sites that went down while a fix was carried out were not the problem. “The bigger concern is the websites that are not down today. Users should be wary of these, as they are clear targets.” Did someone leak the vulnerability and break the embargo? A number of security companies did break the embargo after the leak, according to the PHP Foundation, but Amazon Threat Intelligence said in a blogpost that it had identified a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt dating to four days before the public disclosure.

The benchmark 30-year fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.32% from 7.40% last week, mortgage buyer Freddie Mac said Thursday. One year ago, the average rate was 6.19%. Borrowing costs on 15-year fixed-rate mortgages, often sought by borrowers refinancing a home loan, also eased this week. That average rate slipped to 6.68% from 6.71% last week. A year ago, it was at 5.44%. Rates on home loans are influenced by inflation, Federal Reserve policy and bond-market investors’ expectations for the economy, among other factors. They generally follow the trajectory of the 10-year Treasury yield, which lenders use as a guide to pricing home loans. events.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Startup Battlefield 200: Celebrating outstanding achievements
events.summary: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. This year, TechCrunch Disrupt showcased the incredible talent and groundbreaking ideas of our 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 cohort . Out of thousands of applications, we selected 200 of the most promising startups, each bringing unique innovations to their respective industries. The competition culminated in an electrifying event where these startups had the opportunity to pitch and demonstrate their solutions live over three days. From the top 20 finalists , TechCrunch editorial selected the top five companies that then battled it out for the $100,000 equity-free prize and the coveted Disrupt Cup. The well-deserved win went to Intero Biosystems , with a strong runner-up, Apate . Among the Startup Battlefield 200 were many industry-defining companies exhibiting and pitching on the Showcase Stage. Here are the standouts: Best Showcase Stage pitch by industry group Lola Vision Systems provides a full-stack AI platform delivering sensor fusion, secure communications, and real-time inference on today’s hardware, with purpose-built silicon on the horizon. Krokos Bio is growing nature’s most valuable ingredients, in a way that is cheaper and more reliable, starting with saffron. Rein Security is the security layer for custom-built enterprise agents — the production AI agents running businesses worldwide. Lumai is the optical compute company addressing scalable AI in the inference era. Uhura Bionics has developed a bionic larynx for singing, laughing, and translating emotions. Maka is delivering developmentally curated shows parents trust and kids love — powered by AI. Legali AI is providing a trauma-informed AI legal companion and ecosystem for the middle class and AI-native firms, with a focus on women who’ve faced abuse. Their all-pink, female-focused booth was a standout on the Expo Floor. Visitors would write empowering messages to women on sticky notes and place them on Legali AI’s banner while learning more about the wonderful work they’re doing. Founder Ira Puteri also made a point of coordinating different pink outfits each day. Love the commitment! The Spirit of Disrupt award unanimously goes to Shogher Atanesyan , founder and CEO of Ardook Data . Her journey to the Startup Battlefield 200 is inspiring, with her first exposure to Disrupt as a volunteer back in 2023. She had reached out to the Battlefield team last year, with a simple request to make “Social Impact” a stand-alone category in the Event App. We were happy to oblige, and just a few short months later she applied for the competition. She made it in on her own merits, as the review team loved the concept of capturing real-world household training data from a willing and paid caregiver network. The data is then sold to physical AI and robotics companies in need of it. Atanesyan may be the most selfless founder we’ve seen in five years of managing the Startup Battlefield 200. Specifically, what she did for visitors to San Francisco. She organized dozens of student volunteers to help these startups manage their booths, coordinated numerous items shipped to her house to circumvent steep shipping costs, and hosted a party for these founders at her house. Additionally, she consistently helped founders who had questions in our community Discord and weekly calls. The Startup Battlefield is more than a pitch competition; it’s an opportunity to build relationships with investors, potential customers, and fellow founders to support each other on their entrepreneurial journeys. As we celebrate the achievements of this year’s winners, we are excited to see how they will shape their industries and drive innovation in the months and years to come. Congratulations to all the participants of the Startup Battlefield 200, and a special thank-you to our judges and sponsors for their support in making TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 a resounding success. events.title: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
events.summary: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work. ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows. Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company. That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch. “They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said. Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all in on ChatGPT, it has not settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.” Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. We’ll evaluate those outcomes and use what we learn to guide how we deploy AI across the business,” he said. Uber says OpenAI worked closely with the company on integrating the chatbot. OpenAI has moved quickly to scale up its enterprise business as it competes with its chief competitor, Anthropic. Once known largely as a consumer brand, the ChatGPT creator has swiftly gained a loyal following with business customers, while other AI companies have struggled to keep up. events.title: Canada hit back at Trump tariffs. Now the U.S. alleges possible election interference.
events.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Canada accused Canadian leaders of "openly" describing plans to "influence American politics," doubling down on Ambassador Pete Hoekstra's claims of potential election interference. Why it matters: The accusation further deteriorates Washington's relationship with its northern neighbor under President Trump's costly trade war that's put political pressure on Republicans. Canada targeted its retaliatory tariffs on politically salient states and products ahead of the U.S. midterms. Driving the news: The embassy cited Canada's targeted tariffs as part of the influence accusations laid out in a Wednesday fact sheet . It cited remarks from Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, including an August press conference where she said Canada was "targeting products that will target states in the U.S." She added, "we're being wise and strategic to put political pressure." Joly has echoed that message throughout the trade tensions. The fact sheet also cited Joly's meeting with Democrats. She recently huddled with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. What they're saying: Asked about the accusations during a news conference, Prime Minister Mark Carney said "all of our actions are in the interest of Canadian workers, Canadian families and the future of this economy." Zoom out: The fact sheet also singled out conservative Ontario Premier Doug Ford over a 2025 anti-tariff ad campaign featuring excerpts from a Ronald Reagan speech . It also cited Liberal MP Anthony Housefather's campaigning for Florida Democrat Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz. The memo read, "The Canadian government brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances." Catch up quick: Hoekstra said in a recent podcast interview that American officials were "closely watching" Canada for potential election interference. Joly said last week it was "absolutely not" fair to characterize Canada's actions as election interference. Her visits, she said, were aimed to attract investments. Carney, after cheering Canada's reduced dependence on the U.S. in a speech earlier this month, joked, "Careful, they might think that's election interference," seemingly a jab at Hoekstra. Worth noting: The Trump administration has taken an increasingly antagonistic approach to Canada, from trade tensions to threats over its sovereignty . In August, Trump signed an executive order to rename Lake Ontario, which straddles the U.S.-Canada border, to "Lake America." He's also continuously said Canada should become the "51st state." The big picture: Trump himself has openly weighed in on politics beyond U.S. borders, including during Canada's 2025 election campaign and ahead of Israel's elections this month. On Sunday, Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection just nine days before Israel's national vote. Go deeper: Escalated U.S.-Canada trade talks threaten fallout

events.title: Tesla is prepping a Cybercab onslaught
events.summary: Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now. Disrupt doors open Oct. 13. Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Tesla says it is preparing to launch its shiny gold Cybercab in new markets outside its home of Austin, Texas, in a bid to “literally take over every part of terrestrial transportation.” “We’re starting with getting people from one place to the other, but we want to basically own transportation of any kind on Earth,” Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday. Tesla has previously shown a concept version of a multi-passenger vehicle it calls the “Robovan,” but it’s unclear if Taneja’s bombastic comments mean the company is working on other types of transportation. What was clearer on the call is that Tesla’s Cybercab expansion will begin in Dallas next month and spread to other cities by the end of this year. Tesla already operates robotaxi versions of its Model Y SUV in small fleets in Dallas, Houston, and the Florida cities of Miami, Orlando, and Tampa. The company also said on its earnings call that it will start selling Cybercabs to fleet operators by the end of this year . Broader expansion of the Cybercab could set up a real fight with Waymo, which is currently the market leader for robotaxis in the United States, with more than 4,000 of them deployed across more than a dozen cities. Tesla has argued that its Cybercab is cheaper and easier to build, which should allow it to undercut Waymo and other robotaxi operators on price. But the company has to reach real scale outside Austin in order to prove that point. Tesla said it’s ready thanks to a dramatic increase in the number of miles its self-driving cars have traveled in recent weeks. While that may be true, Tesla was mum on Wednesday about how much money the overall robotaxi effort is bringing in. Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the new ride-hailing business won’t be noticeable in the company’s overall financial figures until the second quarter of 2027, “and probably a big deal by Q3 or Q4 of next year.” Tesla also made a change to its letter to shareholders that further obscures what little visibility there was into its robotaxi business. In Tesla’s second-quarter letter, the company included a chart for “Cumulative Paid Robotaxi Miles.” A close read of that chart showed a 36% decline from the first quarter of the year. In the new letter released on Wednesday, Tesla changed that chart to show “Cumulative Unsupervised Robotaxi Miles” — an indicator of how far the fleet cars are driving, whether or not they have paying riders on board. There wasn’t much more clarity on the call, either. When asked about paid robotaxi miles traveled, Taneja said the company is “seeing utilization improving,” but didn’t offer specifics. Instead, Taneja kept most of his comments generally focused on Tesla’s plans to scale the Cybercab. That included praise for Tesla’s engineering team for creating a vehicle that, according to the manufacturing team, is very easy to build — and build quickly. “They think this is one of the easiest products for them to scale in terms of manufacturing,” he said. “So scaling would not be that much of a challenge.” What might be a challenge, Taneja said, is that Tesla needs to make sure it has “all the regulatory approvals” so it can “start deploying the Cybercabs as fast as we can produce them.” That echoes many previous comments from Musk, who has long claimed that “regulatory approval” was the biggest barrier to Tesla’s robotaxi plans, not technical progress. Musk has always been a bit hazy about what approvals, specifically, he felt were needed. The company has run into a regulatory hurdle this year, though. In September, just hours after Tesla formally launched its Cybercab in Austin, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) opened an investigation into whether the vehicle complies with current federal motor vehicle safety standards. All automakers self-certify that their vehicles conform to these standards, and Tesla has claimed that the Cybercab is compliant. But it is missing features that the current standards require, like a brake pedal and side mirrors. The NHTSA has proposed removing some of these requirements, but that rule change is likely still at least a few months away. Not every Tesla executive agreed on this during Wednesday’s call. Asked about the remaining bottlenecks for a wider robotaxi rollout, Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla’s vice president overseeing autonomy, said they are “not purely regulatory.” “It’s technology-driven,” he said. “We had initially had the robotaxi service from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m., and then expanded to 10 p.m. to 11 p.m, now it’s going to be pretty soon, [to] 2 a.m. So we’re slowly expanding the availability of robotaxi, and that is driven by the capability of the AI software.

events.title: UAE ranks third globally for quality of life satisfaction among the affluent
events.summary: The UAE has been ranked among the top three nations in which investors are satisfied with the quality of life, prompting them to be confident about their financial future , a study from HSBC has found. About 83 per cent of more than 700 high-net-worth individuals surveyed in the Emirates said they were satisfied, placing the country below only Mexico and India, the London-based bank said in the report released at the UAE Wealth Investment Summit in Dubai on Thursday. The study, conducted by French research firm Ipsos, covered nearly 10,000 HNWIs across 10 markets. The UAE's satisfaction is markedly higher than the overall average of 75 per cent, as more than a quarter gave quality of life a perfect score, which was the joint-highest share of any market and well above the global average of 15 per cent, the report said. Nearly 90 per cent of those are also more confident about their financial future, it said. Those in the UAE are also more active when it comes to business plans, with more than a fifth claiming they are launching, acquiring or investing in a new venture, compared with the general average of 17 per cent, HSBC said. “The UAE has built an environment where people and their wealth can thrive, and this research shows it,” said Sami Abouzahr, HSBC’s head of international wealth and premier banking for the Middle East and UAE. “Investors here are confident, ambitious and internationally connected, and they are planning for the long term.” The HSBC study also suggested half of UAE investors expect to receive a significant financial inheritance, compared to 43 per cent globally, while about 58 per cent expect to leave a significant financial legacy to their heirs or other causes. Among those who expect to inherit and were able to estimate its value, the average expected inheritance is around Dh2 million ($545,000), about twice the global figure, with recipients typically expecting to receive it around the age of 52, HSBC said. “A significant transfer of wealth between generations is under way in the UAE and families want to get it right,” said Craig Worobec, HSBC’s head of wealth and premier solutions for the Middle East and UAE. “That means planning early, having open conversations about what wealth is for, and preparing the next generation with the skills and networks to use it well.” Despite the geopolitical uncertainty and economic headwinds, wealth generation and the flow of new money to the UAE continues. The country is a magnet for the ultra-wealthy , as well as global wealth managers and trillion-dollar asset managers. Abu Dhabi and Dubai have been ranked among the top 10 destinations for next-generation wealth, despite the fallout from geopolitical tension and hostility, London-based consultancy Savills said in a report last week . Also last week, a study from Boston Consulting Group showed that net wealth in the UAE is set to jump to $6 trillion by the end of this decade, despite the short-term volatility caused by conflict in the Middle East . “With a highly international population and wealth that spans several countries, the UAE has become a base from which investors manage and grow their wealth around the world,” HSBC said.

events.title: 'I wasn't thinking straight' says five jobs civil servant
events.summary: Kashim Chowdhury wears dark sunglasses, a hat, hoody and gloves as he arrives at court. His face is largely obscured. A civil servant accused of fraudulently juggling multiple public sector jobs has told the court he "wasn't thinking straight" when he allegedly misled future bosses about his employment status. Kashim Chowdhury said he was "in a panic" when he applied for a job at the Department of Health (DHSC), failing to declare he was already working at the Department for the Environment (Defra). The prosecution said he already had three full-time jobs at the time, including roles at the London Borough of Tower Hamlets and East London NHS Trust. The 55-year-old, who is from east London, is on trial accused of nine counts of fraud. He denies acting dishonestly or intending to make a dishonest gain. Chowdhury said he was "in a panic'' because he feared losing his Defra job and was uncertain about his future. He told the jury he was "not paying attention, I was not thinking straight',' when filling out the application. The prosecution said Chowdhury held five jobs on full-time salaries at the height of the alleged deceit. Civil servant faked illness with make-up to juggle five jobs, court hears Published 14 October Civil servant admits he 'made mistakes' juggling five government jobs Published 1 day ago In the spring of 2023, he was employed by the Defra, the UK Health Security Agency, the Food Standards Agency, the Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office. The jury was told that throughout this period he was contracted to work 183 hours a week - more than the number of hours that exist in seven days. Each job paid a full-time wage, with Chowdhury paid £11,000 for a single month's work in 2023. Prosecutors say Chowdhury "exploited" the work-from-home culture which began during the Covid-19 pandemic to hide his multiple jobs and took sick leave from some employers to manage the workload. But Chowdhury told the court he had not wanted the jobs at the DHSC, Department for Business and Trade and the Home Office. He told the jury: ''I sent out a flurry of these applications. The offers for these jobs came all at once. I had discussions with my line managers saying that I did not want these jobs and explained my circumstances. These were all short term and probationary and my priority was to look after my mother.'' He added that around May and June 2022, his mother's health "deteriorated". He said: "That overwhelmed me at the time. It just destroyed me." Chowdhury described the jobs as his "lifeline at the time". "They gave me a link to the outside world and were a distraction from what was going on in my personal life, looking after my mum at that time." The prosecution alleges Chowdhury managed to keep his overlapping jobs secret because he worked entirely remotely. He told his employers he was the sole carer for his elderly mother and the prosecution alleges he "exploited this opportunity". events.title: NVIDIA Unveils Minerva to Bring End-to-End Observability for AI Factories
events.summary: Launched today, NVIDIA Minerva is an AIOps platform built to help teams find problems earlier and keep AI factories productive. It brings together telemetry from infrastructure and AI workloads, then applies purpose-built AI models to turn that data into timely, actionable insight. AI factories are among the most complex operations in the world, with vast numbers of GPUs working across high-speed networks to train models and serve AI applications. At that scale, a single degraded component can slow an entire job. The warning signs may be easy to miss, such as a GPU running hotter than its peers or an NVMe drive losing performance under load. The platform focuses on AI factory yield, a measure of the useful work infrastructure produces through GPU hours, goodput, cluster uptime and token production. Delivering a Dynamic View of an AI Factory Traditional monitoring tools often divide the data center into separate views. Networking, compute, site reliability and machine learning teams each see a different part of the operation. Minerva connects those signals across NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and workloads. With these signals, Minerva builds a dynamic knowledge graph that logically maps the infrastructure — GPUs, SuperNICs, switches and cables — and the jobs running on it. This context helps operators trace a slow training job to the component affecting it, even across a factory with hundreds of thousands of GPUs. It analyzes billions of data points per hour using supervised and unsupervised machine learning. It learns normal behavior, detects previously unseen anomalies, predicts emerging failures and correlates related events based on the factory’s topology. Instead of sending every symptom to an operator, it can group an event storm into a focused incident with a likely root cause. Minerva comes with a native AI assistant and connects to external agentic AI tools. This adds a natural-language interface grounded in live telemetry. Operators can investigate cluster health and receive recommended remediation through conversation. Teams can keep a person in the loop to manually implement fixes or connect Minerva to automation through infrastructure application programming interfaces and external systems. Results That Maximize AI Factory Yield The ability to correlate workload and infrastructure issues along with its agentic AI capabilities help simplify AI factory operations. Instead of dealing with a blizzard of alerts, Minerva aggregates related problems into a single actionable item. This allows AIOps teams to move from reactive to proactive maintenance. And all of this helps AI factories maximize GPU uptime. Minerva delivers value for the key metrics AI factories focus on: Longer time between interruptions : Minerva spots trouble before it happens, so jobs run longer without incident. Faster time to repair : When an incident does happen, Minerva pinpoints the problem, leading to a significantly quicker resolution. Greater insight : Modern AI infrastructure generates a flood of data; Minerva filters it out, leaving only the handful of alerts that actually matter. IREN is among the NVIDIA partners using Minerva to optimize its AI factories. “As we scale our AI factories, the key to providing the best service for our customers is maximizing the productivity of our GPUs,” said Denis Skrinnikoff, chief technology officer of IREN. “NVIDIA Minerva gives our operations team one view across the network, the GPUs and the jobs running on them, so we focus more on proactive maintenance rather than troubleshooting. That visibility strengthens our operating model for the infrastructure we’re building next.” Joining IREN , Aolani , Bitdeer AI , IBM , Jio, Lambda , Quake AI and Tesla plan to deploy Minerva. In addition to Dell Technologies , Lenovo and Supermicro will offer Minerva as part of their AI factory operations portfolios. See notice regarding software product information. events.title: Lawyers for Trump, BBC battle over depositions in president's $10 billion defamation case
events.summary: Lawyers for the BBC and Donald Trump are in court arguing over whether former special counsel Jack Smith should be deposed in Trump’s $10 billion defamation case against the British broadcaster MIAMI -- Lawyers for the BBC and for Donald Trump were tussling in court Thursday over whether former special counsel Jack Smith should be deposed in the president’s $10 billion defamation case against the broadcaster — a possibility that Trump strongly opposes. In a hearing before U.S. Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett in Miami, the parties were also expected to address the thorny issue of when Trump himself will be made available for deposition. BBC asked the judge last week to compel Trump to appear after they said he canceled an agreed-upon date of Oct. 16, citing “matters of national importance.” The British broadcaster says Trump is trying to delay his appearance until January 2027. The judge has threatened sanctions if Trump fails to comply with the court's schedule. Trump, who has often avoided depositions, filed his lawsuit against the BBC last December, seeking $10 billion in damages. He accused the publicly funded broadcaster of defamation as well as deceptive and unfair trade practices related to a documentary, “Trump: A Second Chance.” The BBC acknowledged that filmmakers spliced together quotes from different sections of the speech Trump delivered to his supporters on Jan. 6, 2021, before the storming of the U.S. Capitol, to make it seem he was directly urging violence. The broadcaster apologized over the editing, and the head of the BBC and its top news executive both resigned. But BBC has denied Trump’s claims that it defamed him. To bolster its defense, the broadcaster subpoenaed Smith earlier this month. Trump’s lawyers argued, in a joint filing asking for a hearing on the matter, that there was no good reason for Smith, who is not a party to the case, to appear. “Smith lacks any personal knowledge regarding the issues in this matter,” they argued in the filing. “He was not present when President Trump’s January 6, 2021, speech … was made, nor did he participate in its preparation. Smith does not have any personal knowledge regarding President Trump’s state of mind at the time the Speech was given.” Trump's side also argued that “Smith’s testimony would be duplicative,” because he published he lengthy report on the events of January 6 and also testified for many hours. “The entirety of his testimony is publicly available,” it argued. The BBC countered, in the same filing, that there were few more knowledgeable sources about the events of Jan. 6 than Smith, who studied and investigated them for years. Rep. Ilhan Omar says she will move from her Washington, DC, home after federal search Man hops onto moving school bus when he sees driver in distress Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say “It is difficult to imagine a more authoritative source on these issues than Mr. Smith, who spent years gathering evidence on those topics with the force of the Justice Department and the power of the grand jury behind him,” the BBC’s lawyers argued. “No one forced Plaintiff to file this lawsuit and to dispute that his speech on January 6 incited the violence that followed at the Capitol. But as long as he chooses to maintain the case, he cannot commit the fundamental injustice of preventing the BBC from obtaining the evidence it needs to robustly defend itself on every element of his claim…” A key question also remains: When will Trump himself appear? In a filing Oct. 13, BBC lawyers said they first requested dates for a deposition in July, and followed up repeatedly, with both sides eventually agreeing on Oct. 16. After weeks of silence, they wrote, “Plaintiff’s counsel responded on September 28, 2026, indicating that ‘the President is no longer available for his deposition on October 16 due to other matters of national importance’ and that counsel would ‘endeavor to provide you with a replacement date by the end of this week.’ He did not.” They said they were then told that Trump “has no availability whatsoever for a deposition” before discovery is set to close on Dec. 18, and that Trump would instead make himself available the second or third week of January. “Two months of discovery remaining, the BBC still has not been able to depose, and does not even have a schedule to depose, the most central figure in this case: Plaintiff himself,” attorney Charles D. Tobin wrote in the filing. “Those delays have flouted the cooperative spirit of discovery and precluded the BBC from obtaining the evidence necessary to robustly litigate its defense.” Amy Acton campaign slams Ramaswamy over controversial ad featuring estranged mother 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

events.title: Paid parental leave doesn't strain most employers, survey finds
events.summary: Employers might be overestimating the downsides of offering paid parental leave and underestimating the costs of losing employees by foregoing it, argues economist Emily Oster in a new report based on research she conducted with the advocacy group Healthy Moms, Healthy Babies America. A survey of employers in four states without public-sponsored leave programs — Arkansas, Illinois, Mississippi, and Nebraska — found that 55% of employers reported no additional costs from offering it. In 77% of cases, employers said existing staff absorbed the work of the new parent. Overall, respondents with experience offering parental leave were twice as likely to say the benefits outweighed costs (47% vs. 23%). Some employers cited worker retention as a reason they offered it. “This data suggests it is far more manageable for employers than many people fear,” said Oster, also the CEO of ParentData, a data-driven parenting and pregnancy advice platform. Still, 17% of employers who offered leave said it created “significant financial strain.” The study did not specify the length of the paid leave or examine if there were adverse retention effects on other employees within the company. Oster suggested states should consider tax credits to entice employers to offer parental leave, and should try to increase public awareness of her survey’s results, especially among small businesses. Healthy Moms, Healthy Babies’ push for paid leave research comes as part of a campaign to spend $100 million over five years to advance research and policies to push down the US maternal mortality rate by half, according to Robin Reck, the group’s executive director.

events.title: Vape critics accuse RJ Reynolds of marketing to kids
events.summary: An RJ Reynolds subsidiary is promoting fruit-flavored vaping pods with colorful scented mailers that critics say are similar to the “scratch and sniff” ads the tobacco giant agreed to suspend 20 years ago, as part of a settlement with 39 states that had accused the company of violating an agreement to refrain from marketing its flavored cigarettes to kids. “It appears they haven’t learned their lesson, and they’re now using that same playbook for a different type of tobacco product, which also coincidentally remains the most commonly used tobacco product among US youth,” said Brian King, a former top FDA tobacco regulator who now works as the executive vice president for US programs at the Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids. His organization flagged the materials to state and federal authorities. The company said the advertising for Vuse Pro berry, fresh mint, peach, and watermelon pods was only sent to existing adult nicotine consumers whose ages had been verified, and who had opted in to Vuse-related communications. “Our products are for adult tobacco and nicotine consumers only,” a spokesperson said. “We do not want youth accessing or using them, and that principle is fundamental to how we market responsibly and in compliance with applicable laws and regulations.” Flavored vape policy came to a head earlier this year when President Donald Trump pressured then-FDA Commissioner Marty Makary to authorize fruit-flavored e-cigarettes for adults despite the agency chief’s concerns about the potential impact on children . Shortly after, the FDA adopted a policy that effectively allowed for the sale of many flavored e-cigarettes that were still under agency review. “It’s critical that the US government and state attorneys general take notice and take action,” King said. “We should not be sitting idly by as companies flagrantly flout the laws using tactics we know drive youth appeal of tobacco products.” — David Lim

events.title: Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs as it increases reliance on AI
events.summary: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 staff as it introduces more artificial intelligence (AI) into its work processes. The banking group said 1,000 posts had already been closed and it expects a further reduction of 4,000 to be complete by the end of this year, amounting to around 5% of its global workforce. The bank's cost reductions are focused on its UK retail bank, but some back office functions for the UK are done in India, where a significant proportion of the job cuts are expected to fall. Barclays said the changes were the result of an ongoing modernisation plan, with the use of AI being the "icing on the cake" of its strategy. Although not all of the cuts are due to AI, their scale will prompt further concern over the impact of the new technology. Company spending on AI is increasing along with claims new tools can replace some of the basic tasks currently done by staff such as administrative and programming work. HSBC, Standard Chartered and Danske Bank have also flagged AI-related job cuts this year. "It is a hot button topic," said AJ Bell investment analyst, Russ Mould. However, banks had not yet made big moves towards the widespread introduction of AI and they would be considering the implications for security and customer service before implementing AI technology to make financial savings, he said. "Any company at any time needs to keep on top of its cost base," he said. "It will be intriguing to see what other banks say in their results in the coming weeks. Sharon Graham, general secretary of the Unite union that represents banking sector workers said the company was "using AI as an excuse to discard its loyal and long-suffering workforce". "Employers should be focussed on upgrading employees' skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach," she said. Barclays is reaching the end of a three year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking arm, although the investment banking division is also affected. AJ Bell's Russ Mould said despite "reaching for the AI lever" Barclays had failed to match expectations with its financial results. Barclays also revealed it made £2.3bn profit in the three months to September, higher than the same period a year ago, but slightly less than forecast. Barclays Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were the result of significant investment it is making in technology to simplify and improve its business. "AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future. "We will employ the AI at scale," he said. "But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake. "Because you need to do the infrastructure build to get the benefits of AI." Barclays said around 60% of the job cuts will fall within its support functions, including among developers. Will Howlett, financials analyst at Quilter Cheviot said the cuts illustrated "how significantly AI and automation could reshape the banking industry over the next few years". "Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business," he said. Barclays said it expects its efficiency measures to deliver a further £1.1bn of savings in 2027. How has AI changed your job or the type of work your do? events.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026
events.summary: U.S. Energy Information Administration - EIA - Independent Statistics and Analysis Browse by tag liquid fuels natural gas electricity oil/petroleum production/supply crude oil consumption/demand generation prices map states exports/imports international coal renewables weather forecasts/projections gasoline capacity steo (short-term energy outlook) Data source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Weekly Petroleum Status Report The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel , incentivizing the increased run rates. Since 1991, U.S. refinery utilization has averaged 92% from May to September, compared with 88% across the other seven months. U.S. refineries tend to run at their highest rates between May and September to boost supply of gasoline for the peak demand season in the summer months. Distillate demand, by contrast, peaks in the fall and winter . Because refineries produce a combination of gasoline and distillates, high summer refinery utilization usually leads to an increase in distillate inventories before seasonal refinery maintenance and the peak distillate demand season. This year the refinery runs were driven largely by tight global supplies for distillate fuel oil, leading to high international demand for U.S. distillate fuel oil exports. While refinery utilization was the highest since 1998, total U.S. refinery output was only the highest since 2019 because refining capacity has decreased by 4% since then. In the first 3 weeks of October, U.S. refinery utilization decreased from its summer highs but remained above the five-year (2021–2025) seasonal average. events.title: Data and AI agents give a lift to TK Elevator service technicians
events.summary: DÜSSELDORF, Germany — Torben Teichmann, a service technician for TK Elevator , arrives at an office building. To do maintenance on an elevator, he dons his hard hat, safety glasses and gloves and takes out the tools he needs to access the parts of the elevator the public rarely sees. In the past, Teichmann might have needed to manually find information: ask around to find the elevator, track down the notebook containing handwritten service notes and search through hundreds of pages of technical manuals. He might have discovered he needed other tools, requiring trips back to his car. Once the work was complete, he wrote up his notes, usually in his car, “and it’s not so comfortable to write there.” Today, however, an agentic AI app, created with Microsoft Foundry and Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models , briefs Teichmann through his phone or tablet about the elevator before he even enters the building. He knows which tools to take with him. He knows which elevator, on which floor, and what the issue is — whether it’s regular maintenance or a service call for a problematic door, for example. On his phone, he can search digital manuals or the previous service history of the elevator. “I love AI. It’s really easy. (…) I’m the boss at the job site and the AI is my buddy that gives advice.” Torben Teichmann, a service technician for TK Elevator. Photo by Max Brunnert for Microsoft. Afterward, another AI voice agent asks him questions about the work he has performed, which he can explain in his own words. The debriefing agent records Teichmann’s answers without requiring any writing or typing. It asks follow-up questions if more detail is needed. The exchange works in both directions. The assistant draws on information collected from earlier visits, while Teichmann’s spoken debrief adds his experience to the record for colleagues who may service the equipment later. In the end, his debriefing notes are essential. Not just for him but for future generations of technicians. As TKE has 25,000 highly qualified service technicians globally, there are significant learnings from other parts of the world Teichmann can draw upon. In turn, his learnings will help colleagues across Germany and in other parts of the world. “I love AI,” Teichmann says. “It’s really easy. The best is it’s information I need now,” he adds, pointing his finger to emphasize the urgency . “I’m the boss at the job site and the AI is my buddy that gives advice.” The agents draw on a digital foundation TKE has developed over the past decade by connecting elevators and escalators to the secure cloud and bringing together the connected-equipment data, service information and technical documentation using Microsoft Azure. Based in Düsseldorf, TK Elevator (TKE) manufactures, installs and services elevators and escalators, called “units” in industry parlance. Once purchased, those units are the property of the building owner. TKE has service contracts to maintain them, much the way an individual buys a car and takes it to the dealer for annual checkups. Units can last for decades, so maintenance plays an important role at TKE, whose 25,000 service technicians care for 1.4 million units globally. The work is largely invisible when everything is running. But when an elevator breaks down, it quickly affects how people move through their day. TKE says its units carry 1.5 billion passengers a day. “Our equipment is infrastructure critical,” says Christian Fongern, CEO of TKE Germany. “Imagine in an airport, in a hospital or in an office, an elevator or escalator is not working. This has tremendous impact on the people in that building. Our utmost target is to keep the elevators running. Uptime is our mission critical statement here, and service is the heart of our business.” Most of the work is regular maintenance; not every service call involves a mechanical failure. Everyday use can also cause problems. For example, physical force applied to elevator doors or buttons, chewing gum deposited under an escalator handrail, all manner of small items (keys, coins, baby pacifiers) falling through the gap by the elevator door. Birds and mice manage to enter and make a mess. Dirt tracked in by so many shoes is one of the biggest problems, clogging the door rails or blocking a sensor. Whether the visit is planned or not, AI agents are intended to make the work easier by helping technicians find relevant information more quickly. TKE began digitally connecting elevators and escalators around a decade ago, using sensors and digital controllers to collect information about how the equipment was operating. From the start, it brought that information together in a central data platform using Microsoft Azure , ⁠⁠ Azure IoT and ⁠ Azure Databricks and built it out further in partnership with Microsoft Industry Solutions Engineering , now called Microsoft Frontier Company . Creating a common data environment was particularly important as TKE added different types of equipment through acquisitions. That meant servicing units made by other manufacturers, as well as introducing its digital-native EOX and HELIX elevators. More recently, generative AI has started to allow the company to draw on information that does not sit neatly in operational systems, including technical documents and technicians’ service notes. “Everything we did before was on structured data,” says Christian Jung, head of digital data and AI foundation at TK Elevator. “It was either IoT data or enterprise data sitting in systems already. But we were not able to leverage data from unstructured sources.” Sensor readings can show what an elevator is doing. But much of the knowledge needed to diagnose a problem may be elsewhere: in a technical manual, a previous technician’s notes or a description of what happened during an earlier visit. Generative AI allows TKE to extract, search and draw connections across these sources. “We were able to give technical guidance to technicians on how to fix a problem,” Jung says. For example, the same models of elevators or escalators in different buildings may get very different usage and service history — useful information when it’s time to maintain or repair a unit. Other context — the location of the unit, the business hours, the specific floor having a problem — can save a service technician significant time and frustration. It’s all the kind of information that generative AI can process easily but that was difficult to gather and share before. Collecting the data was only the first step. TKE created nine digital operations centers, or DOCs, where data analysts and technical specialists look for patterns that could help technicians identify emerging problems or prioritize maintenance. Tobias Lüsebrink heads digital transformation for TKE Germany and works at the DOC in Berlin, where data analysts and technical elevator experts work closely to interpret data and find patterns.

events.title: Brazil's energy course may hold after election, but Amazon at risk
events.summary: Brazil’s energy path could change less than environmentalists expect if right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro wins Sunday’s presidential election. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s administration has celebrated new oil discovery and exploration efforts, marking a difference from some regional leftist allies. Lawmakers from the candidates’ respective parties also found much agreement when debating a critical minerals law that centers domestic value addition earlier this year. One area where the pair may diverge, however, is on the Amazon: Brazilian economist Monica de Bolle said the enforcement of existing environmental laws could weaken under Bolsonaro, whose father presided over the loss of more than 11 million acres of rainforest. A nearly $3 billion takeover of a Brazilian rare earth mining firm by USA Rare Earths—which the US government holds a stake in— also hangs in the balance: Lula opposed it, and will likely try to use a new law to change the terms of the deal if he remains in office, according to de Bolle. — Eugenia Perozo

events.title: Climate talks are failing
events.summary: Tim’s view Climate diplomacy is deeply broken. The latest dire United Nations projection, published on Wednesday, stressed that the ambitions to limit global warming adopted a decade ago in Paris are all but out of reach , absent an urgent economic and political pivot that appears nowhere on the horizon. Blowing past 1.5℃ of warming is inevitable, and even the most far-fetched techniques possible to claw temperatures back down probably won’t return it to that level in the future. Warming is instead on track to reach 2.8℃ this century, the report said. And, perhaps even more alarmingly, the report found that even if all countries fulfill the climate plans they’ve spent the past decade honing through the UN negotiating process — a very big if — warming will only be limited to 2.6℃. Setting adequate goals, nevermind achieving them, is itself apparently impossible. Unsurprisingly, the report lays a lot of blame on the US, which saw its emissions rise more than any other country in the past year. But the bigger consequence of the US withdrawal from the Paris process — which will continue with COP31 in Türkiye in a few weeks — is that its leadership was evidently important in maintaining a strong centralized platform for collective action. Instead, Eurasia Group analyst María José Valverde wrote this week, talks have splintered into a miasma of bilateral one-off deals that, collectively, are no more likely to produce stronger climate outcomes and that render “negotiations increasingly unproductive” and COP summits “progressively irrelevant,” especially as governments and companies grapple with a cascading series of energy crises. Türkiye has a chance to change the course. Ankara’s advantage is that its central goal for the summit — accelerating electrification — is also a key principle of energy security. But it’s not enough, on its own, to put Paris back within reach. Notable China is planning to frame tariffs against some of its clean technology as a major obstacle for global climate action in the upcoming COP summit.

events.title: Tank barrel production returns to UK after 20 years
events.summary: Rheinmetall said the facility had created 100 jobs and it would look to expand its workforce in the future The production of gun barrels to be used on tanks has returned to the UK for the first time in 20 years with the opening of a new manufacturing facility. The UK Gun Hall in Telford, run by German defence firm Rheinmetall, has supported 100 jobs and will make barrels and breeches for large calibre weapons. Defence secretary, Wes Streeting, attended the opening ceremony on Thursday and said Britain was "back in the business of making weapons" for its armed forces. "From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action," he said. "One hundred skilled jobs in world class manufacturing and the return of large calibre weapon production to UK soil for the first time in 20 years - this is what defence as an engine for growth looks like," Streeting added. The barrels and breeches will be made for both 120m and 155mm weapon systems, including for the RCH 155 and future artillery platforms, according to Rheinmetall. The firm is already involved in the UK's Boxer combat vehicle programme and is upgrading the country's Challenger tanks . Wes Streeting said the opening of the facility would be a boost to Britain's defence capabilities Specialist workers from Telford have been recruited and the firm said it would expand its workforce as production ramped up. Ahead of the factory's opening, staff spent time at a Rheinmetall facility in Germany where they were trained in precision manufacturing, quality assurance and specialist weapon production. Armin Papperger, CEO of Rheinmetall, said the gun hall was an "important milestone" that would strengthen the country's industrial base "for decades to come". "We are committed to investing in the UK for the long term, expanding our industrial footprint and working together to deliver the capabilities needed for the future," he added. Papperger told BBC Radio Shropshire it was a significant investment in Telford, adding that the firm only had one similar production line in Germany. "At the moment, we have a lot of orders and we need the capacity. Telford has very well-educated people, highly-motivated people," he added. Papperger said the company currently had 1,300 employees in the UK but was looking to build up that number. During his speech at the event, Streeting described Telford as being "synonymous with engineering and manufacturing". "Today is a vote of confidence in our country," he continued, "a statement of intent on our mission to reindustrialise Britain and create good, well-paid jobs across our country." events.title: TSH Resources reports 274 hot spots within estate boundaries after SGX queries over haze
events.summary: Children wearing face masks in Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan province, on Oct 21. TSH Resources operates 36,000ha of planted areas in Kalimantan and Sumatra. SINGAPORE – Plantation company TSH Resources said 274 hot spots were detected within its estate boundaries in Indonesia between Jan 1 and Oct 21, but maintained that none of the fires occurred within its planted or operational areas. The Malaysian plantation group , which has a primary listing on Bursa Malaysia and a secondary listing on the Singapore Exchange (SGX), said all the hot spots were located in community enclaves outside areas directly managed by the company. “The group’s field teams responded to and extinguished these fires, and police reports have been lodged in respect of these incidents,” the plantation group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia and SGX. Its Oct 22 disclosure was in response to queries from SGX Regulation (RegCo) regarding forest and peatland fires in Indonesia which have caused transboundary haze affecting the region. The company operates 36,000ha of planted areas in Kalimantan and Sumatra, according to its 2025 annual report. The company also disclosed that a fire occurred on Aug 17 within an area of its subsidiary, Bulungan Citra Agro Persada (BCAP). It said the fire originated from a community enclave outside BCAP’s operational area, and was extinguished on the same day. BCAP subsequently lodged a police report and continued cooperating with the relevant authorities. Separately, TSH said it received an inquiry from the sustainability department of Apical Group, one of its customers, on Sept 1 concerning hot spots at another subsidiary, Farinda Bersaudara. TSH said it explained that the incident occurred in a community enclave outside its operational area, and that Apical, a vegetable oil processor, was satisfied with its explanation. The company said it had not received any other formal inquiries or notices from the environmental authorities concerning the recent haze. It added that its operations and activities within its Indonesian concessions had not contributed to the transboundary haze. TSH is among eight agribusiness companies listed in Singapore that have responded to queries from SGX RegCo concerning their operations and possible links to the Indonesian fires. The others are Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar International, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri Resources and Olam Group. TSH said it has enforced a zero-burning policy since May 2009, prohibiting the use of fire in land preparation, new planting and replanting activities. The policy also applies to its contractors and suppliers. It added that it had not undertaken new planting on peatland since the end of 2015. To monitor fire risks, the company uses satellite-based monitoring systems to detect hot spots, land clearing and possible encroachment. TSH said it has 123 fire observation towers, 11 drones and 28 firefighting squads comprising 425 firefighters. It spends an average of RM2 million (S$625,200) annually on fire prevention, monitoring and response measures. TSH has continued repurchasing its own shares amid the heightened scrutiny. In a separate filing on Oct 22, the company disclosed that it bought back another 250,000 shares, spending around RM286,577. The purchases brought its cumulative treasury holdings to about 65.6 million shares, equivalent to around 5.1% of its issued shares. In September, TSH disclosed that its 90%-owned indirect Indonesian subsidiary has been fined about RM42 million over the cultivation of land outside the legally approved plantation area.

events.title: War dents Gulf’s protein boom
events.summary: Anyone aiming to boost their protein intake in the Gulf has likely felt the pinch in their wallet lately. Prices are rising everywhere, driven by a global craze to add protein to everything, but this isn’t converting to profits for Gulf food producers, who are grappling with higher costs because of the war. Riyadh-based National Agricultural Development Co., best known for its Nadec dairy brand, doubled sales in its protein segment for a second consecutive quarter, helping lift revenue by 7.8% compared to a year ago. But net profit plunged 72.5% year-on-year because of higher feed prices, shipping costs, and surcharges associated with maritime logistics. Nadec expects the pressure to ease once the “regional operating environment normalizes.” Still, the results show how even businesses with domestic production and strong local demand are struggling with the war’s logistics disruptions. — Mohammed Sergie

events.title: Mark Carney lands in Turkey to forge a new partnership as Canada looks beyond the US
events.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has arrived in Turkey for a two-day visit to forge a new partnership ANKARA, Turkey -- Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in Turkey on Thursday for a two-day visit seeking to forge a new partnership as Canada looks to reduce its dependence on the United States . Carney is making the first bilateral visit by a Canadian prime minister to Turkey, although he traveled to Ankara in July to attend the NATO summit . He is scheduled to meet with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and other officials before traveling to Istanbul for talks with Turkish business groups as the two countries seek to deepen trade ties. The Canadian prime minister has sought to diversify partnerships and reduce reliance on the United States amid an escalating trade war with U.S. President Donald Trump, marked by U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, retaliatory measures by Canada and statements questioning Canadian sovereignty. In an interview with Turkey’s state-run Anadolu Agency, Canada’s Ambassador to Turkey, Marcel Lebleu, said this week that the visit’s main purpose was to “launch a strategic partnership through a joint declaration by the two leaders.” Talks would focus on cooperation in energy, nuclear plants, sustainable mining and the defense industry. The two countries would also hold negotiations on a free-trade agreement, he said. Turkey is looking to build a second nuclear power plant on the Black Sea coast, in addition to one currently being built by Russia’s Rusatom on the Mediterranean coast. Mounted cavalry units escorted Carney's vehicle to the sprawling Turkish presidential compound, where a welcoming ceremony was held. Erdogan and Carney then proceeded to a palace building for bilateral talks. On Thursday, Amnesty International called on Carney to raise human rights concerns during his trip. Rep. events.title: Millions in cheese revenue lost as protest torpedoes Italy's buffalo mozzarella output
events.summary: A truckers' protest in southern Italy has halted the production of buffalo mozzarella, causing an estimated 3 million-euro loss in just 24 hours ROME -- A truckers' protest in southern Italy has halted the production of the famed buffalo mozzarella , causing an estimated loss of 3 million euros in just 24 hours as the milk cannot reach dairies in the Naples region and the finished cheese cannot reach customers, an official said. The weeklong strike by truck drivers over the high cost of diesel driven up by the Iran war has also blocked deliveries of other basic goods to supermarkets and left gas pumps empty in much of southern Italy. The government approved new tax breaks for truckers Thursday, but it was too early to tell whether they were enough to end the protest. The disruption is particularly damaging to buffalo mozzarella because the production of the protected cheese depends on a tightly timed supply chain. Buffaloes have to be milked regardless of whether dairies are operating, while production rules require that their milk be turned into mozzarella within 60 hours. Pier Maria Saccani, director of the Consortium for the Protection of Mozzarella di Bufala Campana DOP, said that about 1 million liters of buffalo milk produced on Wednesday couldn't be turned into mozzarella because of the transport blockade. The consortium oversees production standards and protects the designation of origin of the cheese in Italy and abroad. “Yesterday, no mozzarella was produced,” Saccani said, explaining it was a “3 million-euro block in 24 hours” — a loss of about 3.4 million dollars. Farmers typically have only enough capacity to hold the fresh milk until dairy trucks collect it and cannot store large quantities for extended periods. “So this blockade has obviously caused panic among farmers, who say, ‘Where are we going to put it?’” Saccani added. The dairies making mozzarella cannot afford to accumulate a highly perishable product if trucks are unable to deliver it to customers. Several dairies have remained closed as a result, Saccani said, describing the situation as a “complete production blockade.” Unlike false claims this summer that production of Parmigiano Reggiano cheese was in crisis due to extreme heat, buffalo mozzarella output is indeed in jeopardy. Rep. Ilhan Omar says she will move from her Washington, DC, home after federal search Man hops onto moving school bus when he sees driver in distress Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say During an extraordinary Cabinet meeting on Thursday, the Italian government led by Premier Giorgia Meloni approved new measures to help truckers and farmers face higher fuel costs, bringing financial aid to those two groups to a combined 540 million euros in tax credits, up from 434 million euros. Some farmers have resorted to feeding part of the unused milk to their animals because they have nowhere to send it, Saccani said, adding that the transport disruption is also threatening supplies of animal feed and diesel needed to keep farms operating. “It’s a very, very complex and delicate situation,” he said. The blockade comes as milk producers and dairies are already confronting higher costs. Saccani said the consortium estimates production costs have risen about 30%, driven by increases in animal feed, diesel, energy, plastic packaging and transportation. The increases have not been fully passed on to customers, he said, leaving producers to absorb much of the additional expense and cutting into profitability across the supply chain. Buffalo mozzarella is an important industry in the Campania region, where the city of Naples is located, and in neighboring areas of southern Italy. Saccani said that in 2025, the production of Mozzarella di Bufala Campana DOP totaled just under 58,000 metric tons, with about 37% of production exported. France is its largest foreign market. events.title: Dubai introduces one frequent flyer mile for each minute in the city
events.summary: The airline points game has been over for years, but the marketing gimmicks refuse to die. Emirates, which has nearly returned to its prewar capacity, is trying to entice more connecting travelers on long-haul flights to make a stop in Dubai. Previous incentives included discounts at amusement parks, hotels, and restaurants, but now it’s adding a sweetener: one frequent-flier mile for each minute spent in the city. The fine print matters, however, as the maximum award is 7,200 points for a five-day visit . While this is a bonus for anyone already planning to come, it’s hard to justify extending a stay, even by a minute. The most travelers can earn converts to a 216 dirham ($59) voucher at Dubai Duty Free, and is nowhere close to a cabin upgrade. — Mohammed Sergie

events.title: The Briefing Room
events.summary: Radio 4 , · 22 Oct 2026 , · 28 mins Will the French accept that changes need to be made to fix their ailing economy? But there are some serious economic issues that must be faced head on. France's borrowing costs have just hit a 26 year high, signalling they are not trusted to manage their growing debt. Public spending in France is higher than in many other European countries and a big part of that bill is pensions. Raising the pension age would save the state much needed money but proposals to do so were met with outrage and put on hold. So, has France become ungovernable? events.title: UAE nominates Lana Nusseibeh to become next UN secretary-general
events.summary: The UAE nominated Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Lana Nusseibeh to become the next UN secretary-general, entering a crowded race to succeed António Guterres when his term ends in December. Born in 1978, Nusseibeh is an Emirati citizen whose family traces its roots to one of the most prominent Muslim dynasties in Jerusalem. She became the UAE’s ambassador to the UN in 2013 and led the country’s delegation during its 2022-2023 term on the Security Council. “Her candidacy stands as confirmation of the importance Gulf states still place on the UN in their ambitious future planning,” Kristin Smith Diwan recently wrote for the Washington-based Arab Gulf States Institute. If selected, Nusseibeh would become the second Arab to lead the UN, after Egypt’s Boutros Boutros-Ghali, and its first woman. — Mohammed Sergie

events.title: AI-related demand powers prices, rents of Singapore industrial space in third quarter of 2026
events.summary: JTC’s all-industrial rental index rose 0.5% quarter on quarter in the third quarter of 2026, while prices picked up 1% on the quarter and 4.2% year on year. AI-related demand kept Singapore industrial rents and prices firm in Q3 2026, even as occupancy slipped to 88.9%, JTC said on Oct 22. JLL and Knight Frank said semiconductor and manufacturing growth supported demand, but lease renewals, cost-cutting and geopolitical tensions limited stronger occupancy gains. JTC expects around 300,000 sq m of new space in Q4 and 1.2 million sq m a year from 2027 to 2030, while investment sales rose to about $2 billion. SINGAPORE – Buoyant growth in artificial intelligence-related sectors fuelled demand for Singapore industrial space in the third quarter, keeping rents and prices firm even as occupancy dipped. JTC’s all-industrial rental index rose 0.5% quarter on quarter, continuing an upward streak of rents steadily rising for 24 quarters since the trough in the third quarter of 2020. Q3 rents were 2.1% higher year on year, the industrial landlord’s report showed on Oct 22. Prices of industrial real estate also continued to rise , climbing 1% on the quarter and 4.2% year on year. The overall occupancy rate eased 0.2 percentage point from the previous quarter to 88.9%, weighed down by tenants vacating older factories earmarked for redevelopment and weaker demand for suburban business parks. JLL South-east Asia head of research and consultancy Chua Yang Liang said global demand for semiconductors supported the growth of industrial rents. “Asia-Pacific economies including South-east Asia countries like Singapore and Malaysia are firmly plugged into this growth driver,” he added. “Consequentially, Singapore’s islandwide industrial property market continues to maintain a stable rental growth trend, mirroring the growth rate of the previous quarter.” Tridiana Ong, head of occupier strategy and solutions at Knight Frank Singapore, indicated advanced estimates showing that Singapore’s economy grew by 5.4% year on year in Q3 2026. The manufacturing sector expanded by 7.5%, reflecting continued strength in activity, particularly from AI-related industries. Still, the quarterly increase in leasing transactions for multi-user factory and warehouse space was “relatively measured”, Ong said. This suggests that much of the demand stemmed from lease renewals and ongoing space requirements, rather than expansionary moves, she added. Chua also noted that ongoing geopolitical tensions are starting to weigh on occupier sentiment, with cost-cutting and space optimisation efforts beginning to impact overall occupancy levels, although underlying industrial demand continues to be firm. Rental growth is likely to remain modest, he said. He estimated that overall, rents may undergo an upside of 2% to 3% for the full year, given stronger near-term economic performance and continual appetite for premium assets. Chua also anticipated prices rising 3% to 4% as capital continues to flow into safe havens such as Singapore, driving further marginal yield compression. Business park rents inched up 0.1% on the quarter, while occupancy slipped 0.7 percentage point to 77.2%. Warehouse space recorded 1 per cent quarter-on-quarter growth in rental and an 89.7% occupancy rate for the quarter. Rents at multiple-user factory spaces, single-user factory spaces, business parks and warehouses recorded a year-on-year uptick of 1.6%, 3.1%, 0.7% and 2.8%, respectively. With office rents in the Central Business District remaining significantly higher and prime office supply limited, business parks could offer possible space solutions even though CBD locations remain favoured, noted Ong. Citing a “good pipeline supply” of new industrial space, JTC said that as at end-September, around 300,000 sq m of such space could be completed in Q4. Between 2027 and 2030, an average annual supply of 1.2 million sq m of industrial space is expected to be completed, of which 59% is single-user factory space with pre-committed demand. This is slightly higher than an average annual supply of new completions of around one million sq m over the past three years. In Q3, JTC awarded two tenders, one for a single-user development at 6 Tuas Avenue 14, and another for a multiple-user development at 5 Tuas Avenue 13, with bids received reflecting “strong market interest in multiple-user sites”, it said. The tender for another single-user development at Jalan Besut was not awarded as the top bid of $500 per sq m per plot ratio did not cross the reserve price. Across the market, total investment sales value jumped from an estimated $1.4 billion to about $2 billion, driven by a few large-ticket deals alongside sales from newly launched strata industrial developments, said Ong.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives on GeForce NOW at launch, bringing a new campaign, multiplayer action and DMZ, high-stakes extraction mode to supported devices . The campaign also gets an enhanced look: GeForce RTX 5080-class performance arrives for Ultimate members, bringing support for ray-tracing features in the cloud. There’s a new way to join the cloud, too: Existing supported Fire TV Stick users can now purchase one-month Performance or Ultimate memberships directly through Amazon, making it easier to sign up and start streaming on the big screen. Plus, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE brings cinematic pixel art and strategic battles to the cloud, and The Elder Scrolls Online’s Echoes of Skyrim Season adds the entire Greymoor Chapter free for all ESO Standard Edition owners. It’s all part of six games joining the GeForce NOW library this week. Squad up and answer the call on the cloud. Activision and Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches today on GeForce NOW. Members can drop into the trenches in Korea, close-quarter combat in New York, high-octane chases through Paris, night raids in Mumbai and city-wide engagements to reclaim occupied territory. Fight as Private Park, a young South Korean soldier facing live combat for the first time alongside his squad as a routine patrol turns into a desperate fight for survival. Beyond the front lines, operator-turned-outlaw Captain Price is operating outside the system he once served, pursuing revenge through covert missions as the conflict spreads. Multiplayer pairs precise combat with fluid movement, a dozen core 6v6 maps from around the world and battlegrounds that are shaped by the campaign’s global conflict. Loot, fight, negotiate, betray and extract — it’s all fair in the cloud and battleground. Ultimate members can now experience the campaign with ray tracing, powered by newly added GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, handhelds, mobile devices, browsers, supported TVs and more. Members can stream supported PC games they already own or purchase new titles from digital stores including Steam, Epic Games Store, Ubisoft Connect, Xbox PC Game Pass, GOG and EA. The library includes thousands of ready-to-play games, including many of the world’s most-played titles and more than 100 free-to-play games. No downloads, installs, patches or updates stand between a new game and playtime. An Amazon Fire TV Stick, the GeForce NOW app and an Ultimate membership are all it takes to level up the living room with GeForce RTX 5080-powered gaming. Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE launches today on GeForce NOW, bringing the series’ classic roots into a cinematic pixel-art world. Travel with companions bound by fate and uncover the truth behind a force threatening to bring everything to ruin. Strengthen the party with Visions of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, each bringing unique skills and abilities to battle. Dynamic camera angles and pixelized 3D models give familiar fantasy a fresh perspective. Exploit enemy weaknesses to stagger foes, break their defenses and seize extra turns before finishing the bonus phase with powerful Resonance attacks. Airships, crystals, espers and moogles bring familiar series favorites to a world filled with secrets to discover.
